about: POST-HOC (round 17, written after S1v3's results were known; docs/token-saver-benchmark.md deviation S1v3-2). Strict rubrics for the 8 report tasks: each item keeps its registered `line` regexes, adds a required correct-value or defect-statement regex where the registered item scored the topic alone, and lists `not` regexes a matching unit must not match (negations and wrong values). `field: "failing"` items score only the entries of the answer's JSON `failing` array. `controls` are same-topic wrong answers, one negated and one with wrong values, per task; each must score at most 1 item under its strict rubric (saver.test.mjs). The registered rubrics in tasks-saver.json are unchanged and the registered verdicts stand.

controls.negated:
On macOS secrets are not stored in secrets.json; they stay in the Keychain.
The file is not created with mode 0600, rather than 0600 it uses 0644.
Writes are not atomic: there is no temp file and no rename.
There is no fsync; sync_all is never called.
There is no lock file: no advisory lock or secrets.lock is used.
Secrets saved by older versions are never migrated; they stay in the Keychain.
The old Keychain items are never deleted or removed.
Linux and Windows do not use Secret Service or Credential Manager; they use the same file.
PANDACODE_SECRETS_FILE is ignored.
PandaCode is signed with an Apple Team ID, so the Keychain never re-prompts.
controls.wrongValue:
On macOS secrets are written to credentials.json with mode 0644.
Each write goes straight into the file in place, and is flushed with flush() only.
Concurrent writers are kept apart by a SQLite transaction.
Old secrets are read from the SQLite database once and then dropped from it.
Linux uses KWallet and Windows uses DPAPI; PANDACODE_SECRETS_DIR moves the file.
The Keychain was dropped because it was slow.

controls.negated:
There is no limit on entries per task; the old 50 cap was removed.
Text has no size limit, not even 128 KiB.
Attachments have no size limit; the 1 MiB cap was dropped.
Entries are kept only in memory in the webview, not in the queued_messages table.
add puts a new entry at the front, not at the back: position = MIN(position)-1.
take does not remove the entry; it marks it sent.
restore puts the entry back at the end of the queue (MAX(position)+1), not the front.
restore does not skip the 50-entry limit; it enforces the 50 cap like add.
controls.wrongValue:
A task holds at most 100 queued entries.
Text may be up to 64 KiB.
Attachments may be up to 10 MiB encoded.
Entries live in localStorage under pandacode.queue.
add inserts at position 0, the front.
take copies the entry and leaves the row until the send succeeds.
restore inserts at the back of the queue.
restore checks the 100-entry limit again.
